StackType.issue: PowerStackType.Single, and the sim overrides on_stack to `pass` citing it. Per the settled census (`py tools/audit/power_census.py stack`) that reasoning is wrong: Single means "Amount is hidden and is always 1" (PowerStackType.cs:10-13) and PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236) adds unconditionally with no StackType branch. DORMANT here for a reason specific to this power and worth stating: Soar's multiplier reads `DynamicVars["DamageDecrease"]`, NOT Amount (SoarPower.cs:29), so no C# behaviour depends on the amount either. The only ported applier applies it once and removes it on the dive (monsters/glory/owl_magistrate.py:59-60; OwlMagistrate.cs:134 apply, :146 PowerCmd.Remove<SoarPower>). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ModifyDamageMultiplicative.rationale: Constant checked: C# returns `DynamicVars["DamageDecrease"].BaseValue / 100m` and CanonicalVars declares `new DynamicVar("DamageDecrease", 50m)` (SoarPower.cs:17), i.e. exactly 0.5, which is what powers.py:3071 hard-codes. 0.5 is dyadic, so it is outside hook_dispatch G9's float-product problem (`py tools/audit/power_census.py multipliers` lists it as dyadic). `target != base.Owner -> 1m` matches powers.py:3070. The `!props.IsPoweredAttack() -> 1m` guard is carried separately below.

guards.rationale: The sim omits the per-power test and relies on the PIPELINE-level gate instead: cmds.py:56-58 runs modify_damage_additive/modify_damage_multiplicative only when `is_powered_attack(props)` (valueprops.py:47-49, Move && !Unpowered). C# never gates the dispatcher -- CreatureCmd.cs:261 calls Hook.ModifyDamage with ModifyDamageHookType.All for every damage type and Hook.ModifyDamageInternal (Hook.cs:2515-2538) calls every listener -- so the gate lives in each override. Equivalent HERE because this power's C# override does self-gate. The hoisting itself is damage_pipeline gap G3 and is not re-verdicted per rule 3. Independently reproduced: `py tools/audit/power_slot_probes.py ungated-modifiers` finds 37 gated vs 9 ungated C# Modify{Damage,Block}{Additive,Multiplicative} overrides. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.what: Hard-coding 0.5 where C# reads a DynamicVar
guards.rationale: The sim has no DynamicVar system, so the canonical default (50) is inlined as 0.5. Observably identical today; it would diverge if anything ever wrote DynamicVars["DamageDecrease"] at runtime, and nothing in the decompiled source does (the key is only read, SoarPower.cs:11/29). Same shape as FlutterPower's.
